notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is an 11-page primary report of completed replication analyses titled Data-analytic replication attempt to evaluate 5 claims from Hiskey_CompPolitStu_2018_AYQG. It identifies replication team Esteban Méndez Chacón, SCORE RR ID 6m33m and OSF project n7m39. Header identifies download qfh2r and matching OSF project title. References identify Hiskey and Moseley, Severed Linkages: Distorted Accountability in Uneven Regimes, Comparative Political Studies 51(10), 1314–1350, DOI 10.1177/0010414017740603 (2018). This supports replication project identity, but not independent verification of the input broader team/date. This is not merely an abstract or preregistration. No PDF was supplied. Original primary source unassigned and not inspected. No study identifier, description, or locator selects among the five claim tests for row 2067. No target assigned by row order or numerical matching. Candidates: kzd8kn, gubernatorial sociotropic interaction, Table R.1, analytic N 543, logistic coefficient -0.008, SE 0.032, p = 0.804, not replicated; l8rz5d, presidential sociotropic interaction, Table R.2 model (1), N 7,013, coefficient 0.000, SE 0.002, p = 0.905, not replicated; 6rp9on, presidential sociotropic interaction, Table R.2 model (2), N 3,238, coefficient 0.002, SE 0.003, p = 0.460, not replicated; 3n6x9n, presidential security interaction, Table R.2 model (3), N 2,279, coefficient -0.012, SE 0.005, p = 0.014, replicated; w7r4vl, presidential security interaction, Table R.2 model (4), N 2,042, coefficient -0.013, SE 0.006, p = 0.020, replicated. Each p is printed as exact and two-tailed. Ns are explicitly replication analytic sample sizes on p. 2 and observations in Tables R.1/R.2; they are survey respondent observations in separate models, not groups to sum. Exclusions are not specified in those sections; no N derivation used. For 3n6x9n the result sentence inconsistently calls its interaction sociotropic, whereas criteria and Table R.2 identify security. The printed effects are logistic regression coefficients; no standardisation or conversion inferred for ser_method. Differing claim-specific verdicts cannot identify row-specific reported success; no aggregate mixed verdict assigned.
